title: How are the product, HCF and LCM of two numbers linked?
description: The numbers one hundred five and ninety five are broken into primes, and their highest common factor, lowest common multiple and product are found. The product is then matched with the highest common factor times the lowest common multiple. Keeko doubts this and multiplies the two numbers to get the lowest common multiple.
teaching_notes: One idea: the product of two numbers equals their highest common factor times their lowest common multiple. Watch for students who give the product as the lowest common multiple, counting the shared prime twice.

source: For 105 and 95, find the HCF, the LCM and the product, and check that the product equals HCF times LCM.
video_script.why: The child can find the highest common factor and lowest common multiple from primes and now sees how they link to the product.
video_script.substitution: Break each number into primes, read off the HCF and LCM, and multiply to compare with the product.
video_script.anchor: The prime factorisations of one hundred five and ninety five written one under the other, as in the book.
video_script.wrong_answer: multiply the two numbers for the lowest common multiple
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko multiplies one hundred five and ninety five, but the shared five is then counted twice.
video_script.payoff_line: The product equals the highest common factor times the lowest common multiple

final_answer.spoken: the highest common factor is five, the lowest common multiple is one thousand nine hundred ninety five, and the product is nine thousand nine hundred seventy five, which is five times one thousand nine hundred ninety five

never_show: 9975 as the lowest common multiple, marked right
maths_rules: HCF = 5, the only prime in both
9975 = 105 × 95, so the product equals HCF × LCM
slip: 9975 counts the shared 5 twice, so it is 5 times the LCM
video_script.design: One idea: the product equals the highest common factor times the lowest common multiple. The two factorisations stay on the board from step one to the check.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>We take the numbers one hundred five and ninety five.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>We find the largest number that divides both. We find the smallest number that is a multiple of both. We also multiply the two numbers.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Which prime goes into both one hundred five and ninety five?

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

marks.m1: the word prime appears with three small prime numbers

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Every number can be broken into primes, which are numbers whose only factors are one and itself.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The largest number that divides both is called the highest common factor.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The smallest number that is a multiple of both is called the lowest common multiple.

marks.m1: the given line is written in the working band

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Given, the numbers are one hundred five and ninety five.

beats.on_screen: To find: HCF, LCM and product of 105 and 95; check product = HCF × LCM

marks.m1: the find line is written under the given line

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>We have to find the highest common factor, the lowest common multiple and the product. Then we check that the product equals the first times the second.

marks.m2: 95 is broken into 5 × 19 and the shared 5 is lit

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, break both numbers into primes. One hundred five is three times five times seven.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Ninety five is five times nineteen. The prime five is in both.

marks.m1: the shared 5 is written as the HCF
marks.m2: 3, 5, 7 and 19 are joined, each prime once

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, only the prime five is in both, so the highest common factor is five.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The lowest common multiple takes each prime as many times as it appears most. That is three, five, seven and nineteen.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Three times five times seven is one hundred five. One hundred five times nineteen is one thousand nine hundred ninety five.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, the product is one hundred five times ninety five. One hundred five times one hundred is ten thousand five hundred.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Take away one hundred five times five, which is five hundred twenty five.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>That leaves nine thousand nine hundred seventy five.

marks.m2: it is set beside 105 × 95 = 9975 and an equals sign joins them

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, multiply the highest common factor by the lowest common multiple. Five times one thousand nine hundred ninety five is nine thousand nine hundred seventy five.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>This is the same as the product, so the check works.

marks.m1: the HCF 5 and the LCM 1995 are boxed
marks.m2: the product 9975 and its link to 5 × 1995 are written and boxed
marks.m3: the rule product = HCF × LCM is written and boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>The highest common factor is five. The lowest common multiple is one thousand nine hundred ninety five.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The product, nine thousand nine hundred seventy five, is five times one thousand nine hundred ninety five.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The product equals the highest common factor times the lowest common multiple.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the two factorisations
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: LCM = 105 × 95 = 9975; the two 5s in 3 × 5 × 7 × 5 × 19 are lit; the bubble is struck out and 1995 returns

marks.m2: the two 5s in the long product are lit
marks.m3: the bubble is struck out and the LCM 1995 returns

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Keeko thinks we multiply the two numbers for the lowest common multiple. That gives nine thousand nine hundred seventy five.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>But five is in both numbers, so the product counts five twice.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>It counts five once, so the lowest common multiple is one thousand nine hundred ninety five.
